newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Briton sails back home to mark Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Briton sails back home to mark Hong Kong handover.

text.p: Briton Marc Cuthbert set sail on Sunday in a traditional Chinese junk on a voyage from Hong Kong to London to mark the return of the British colony to China this year.
"I'm fully confident. I wouldn't dare otherwise and I have got other people's lives at stake, not just my own. We have taken full precautions," Cuthbert, 33, told reporters before setting sail.

The 18-metre Precious Dragon, one of the few remaining traditional junks in the territory, will take Cuthbert and his crew across the Indian Ocean, the Arabian Gulf, through the Suez Canal, across the Mediterranean and on to England.
Cuthbert, who spent his life savings on the journey, bought the junk five years ago and began preparing for the trip last year.
Precious Dragon left Hong Kong under overcast skies on Sunday morning escorted by well-wishers and the British Navy patrol ship HMS Plover.
If all goes as planned, Cuthbert and his crew of five will arrive in London on July 1 just hours after the colony officially reverts to Beijing's rule after more than 150 years as a British colony.
